TF216414.headline: A dinosaur egg that hatches bubbles
overview: The TF216414 is built as a cracked dinosaur egg: an eggshell housing moulded with an irregular break pattern, and a cut-out window across the front that shows a small prehistoric scene inside it, with dinosaurs standing among ferns and a volcano. Bubbles leave through the opening at the top of the shell, so the unit reads as an egg that keeps hatching rather than as a machine with a nozzle. It is supplied in three colourways, a pale blue, a cream and a lavender, and the model name specifies lights and music as part of the product.

The packing data is what makes this the lowest-commitment item in the collection. One carton holds 72 pieces at 0.254 CBM, and the 216-piece minimum is exactly three cartons, or 0.762 CBM in total. Because 72 divides evenly across the three colours, the minimum can ship as 24 blue, 24 cream and 24 lavender, which is enough to fill a shelf with all three variants from a single order. For scale, a 20GP takes 110 of these cartons, 7,920 pieces, so the minimum order is a small corner of a container rather than a container decision.

Against the other bubble models the position is clear. The TF213393 at $1.58 and MOQ 600 is the volume eight-hole machine; the TF216414 at $2.65 is the shaped novelty tier that carries a gift or party-favour look for a dollar more; the TF200892 at $4.34 and the TF213293 at $6.67 are the two standing outdoor units. A buyer assembling a display usually takes this one to fill the low shelf and to have something that photographs differently from the standard machines next to it.
visible_features: Egg-shaped housing moulded with a cracked-shell break pattern rather than a smooth shell
Front cut-out window showing a prehistoric scene with dinosaurs, ferns and a volcano
Bubble outlet at the top of the egg, so bubbles rise out of the shell
Three colourways: pale blue, cream and lavender
Sold in sealed-box packing, 72 pieces per carton

TF200888.headline: The event-hire sunflower: a pot, a stem, a perforated head
overview: The TF200888 is a sunflower built as a self-supporting unit. A yellow flower head with a perforated centre disc sits on a green stem with two leaves, and the stem is planted in a green pot that acts as the base. The bubble output comes from the perforated disc in the middle of the flower rather than from a separate nozzle, so the head itself is the emitter and the whole silhouette stays recognisable while the unit is running. The model is listed as the Professional Event Edition, which is the way it is positioned commercially: as equipment that a venue, an events company or a party planner puts out repeatedly rather than as a toy bought once.

The logistics support that use. A carton holds 48 pieces at 0.232 CBM and 20.9 kg gross, which is 0.44 kg per unit and light enough that the pot does not make the carton awkward to handle. The 96-piece minimum is two cartons, 0.464 CBM, so a first order can go straight to a venue without a freight decision. At full container the numbers are 120 cartons, 5,760 pieces, on a 20GP.

Inside the collection this is the mid point between two very different things. The TF213393 at $1.58 is the eight-hole volume machine sold in six hundreds. The TF213303 at $5.65 is the pole-mounted sunflower stand that puts the flower at child height in a garden. The TF200888 sits between them: it has the same flower idea as the TF213303 but keeps the planted-pot form, which is what you want on a table, a bar top or a shop counter where a floor stand would be in the way.
visible_features: Sunflower head with a perforated centre disc, which is where the bubbles come out
Green stem with two moulded leaves
Green pot moulded as the base of the unit, so it stands without a pole or bracket
Single-piece body with no assembly between pot, stem and head
Carton packed 48 pieces, 0.44 kg per piece gross

TF212709.headline: Two blasters, one clear, one black
overview: The TF212709 ships as a pair. One unit is moulded in black, the other in a transparent blue shell that shades to pink toward the rear, and the transparency is the point of the second one: the internal mechanism is visible through the casing while the unit fires. Both carry ICE BURST moulded along the receiver and Icy Blaze on the module above it, and both take a detachable box magazine that locks into the base of the grip, shown separately in the product photographs so a buyer can see the part that gets lost first. The muzzle end carries a slotted silencer, and the body is moulded in ABS rather than a soft plastic.

Because it is sold as a set, the carton maths is per pair. A carton holds 18 pieces, nine sets, at 0.241 CBM and 22.5 kg gross, which works out at 1.25 kg per set. The 108-piece minimum is six cartons, 54 sets, and 20GP capacity is 116 cartons, 2,088 pieces. That weight per set is the highest in the water toy range here, so a buyer planning air freight should look at it before locking a price; by sea the density is an advantage, since 0.241 CBM per carton means the container fills on cube rather than on weight.

The commercial case for a two-gun pack is that it removes the single-unit objection. A parent buying a water toy for two children, or a retailer building a gift set, does not have to buy twice, and the display gets two different finishes from one SKU. It belongs to the same Ice Burst line as the TF212706 Aurora single gun, so a buyer can take the single for trial and the pair for the shelf without introducing a second design language.
visible_features: Two blasters per set: one black, one transparent blue shading to pink
Transparent casing on one unit, so the mechanism is visible while it fires
Detachable box magazine at the base of each grip, shown as a separate part in the photographs
Slotted silencer moulded at the muzzle
ICE BURST and Icy Blaze markings on the receiver and the upper module
ABS body, 1.25 kg per set gross

TF213395.headline: A rocket that clamps to a bicycle handlebar
overview: The TF213395 is a rocket-shaped bubble machine designed to be mounted, not held. The body is a white cylinder with a navy nose and moulded tail fins, and a clamp bracket underneath lets it sit on a bicycle handlebar, which is the arrangement shown in the product photographs: the unit is locked onto the bar and the bubble outlets at the nose point forward over the front wheel. The nose carries a cluster of outlets rather than a single hole, and a red light sits behind them. It ships in a colour box printed with a space theme, and the box content includes two 50 ml bottles of bubble water and a small remote control, so the unit is complete out of the carton.

The packing is the tightest in the bubble range. One carton holds 48 pieces at only 0.114 CBM, 18 kg gross, which is 0.38 kg per unit. The 240-piece minimum is five cartons, and a 20GP takes 245 cartons, 11,760 pieces, so the model is cheap to move by sea even though the carton count looks high. The supplied bubble water is the constraint to plan around, not the cube: it is a liquid in the carton, so check the destination market's rules on shipping toys with fluid before you commit to a large order.

Commercially this is a bicycle-accessory product as much as a toy. It gives a bike shop, a cycling retailer or a sports chain a bubble item that belongs in their category rather than in the toy aisle, and the remote means the rider does not have to reach the unit while moving. Within this collection it is the only model that mounts to something else; the TF216414 and the TF213393 are floor or table units, and the two garden-lamp models are ground-standing.
visible_features: Rocket body, white with a navy nose and moulded tail fins
Clamp bracket underneath for bicycle handlebar mounting
Cluster of bubble outlets at the nose with a red light behind them
Supplied with two 50 ml bottles of bubble water and a remote control
Space-theme printed colour box
Carton packed 48 pieces at 0.114 CBM, 0.38 kg per piece gross

TF213301.headline: The garden lamp with a remote, in four colours
overview: The TF213301 is a standing garden light that makes bubbles. A decorated bulb head sits above a clear funnel, the funnel sits on a white pole with a coloured band at the joint, and the pole stands in a round weighted base. The bulb head is moulded with a lattice pattern and a small light on top. Four colourways are produced, blue, purple, green and pink, and the base and pole band are colour-matched to the head, so a set of four reads as a matched garden lighting scheme rather than as four different products. A remote control is included and is shown being operated in the product photographs.

The packaging explains the ordering pattern. A carton holds 36 pieces at 0.28 CBM and 29.2 kg gross, 0.81 kg per unit, and the carton dimensions are identical to the TF213303 sunflower stand: same carton, same cube, same weight. That matters because the two models can be mixed in one container without recalculating the loading plan. The 720-piece minimum is the largest in this collection, 20 cartons and 5.6 CBM, so this is a programme order rather than a trial: 5.6 CBM is a fifth of a 20GP, which holds 100 cartons or 3,600 pieces of this model.

That minimum is the decision. If you want to test the standing garden format, the TF213303 at the same $5.65 has a 180-piece minimum on the same carton, so it is the cheaper way in. The TF213301 earns its minimum when the buyer already knows the format sells and wants the wider colour range plus the remote: four matched colours with a remote is what a garden centre or an outdoor living retailer will put out as a set, and it is the version that photographs as a coordinated product family.
visible_features: Lattice-moulded bulb head with a light on the top cap
Clear funnel section directly under the head, where the bubbles leave the unit
White pole with a coloured joint band, standing in a round weighted base
Four colourways with matching pole band: blue, purple, green and pink
Remote control supplied with the unit
Carton identical to the TF213303 sunflower stand: 36 pieces, 0.28 CBM, 0.81 kg per piece

TF213303.headline: The cheap way into the standing format
overview: The TF213303 puts a sunflower on a pole. A yellow flower head sits at the top, a clear bulb-shaped funnel sits under it, and a green pole with a coloured joint band carries the whole thing down to a round green base. Bubbles are released from the centre of the flower and drift forward across the ground rather than rising straight up, which is why the model is photographed with children running through the stream at lawn height. The housing is moulded in a single green finish, so unlike the four-colour TF213301 this is one look, not a set.

It is built on the same stand as the TF213301 and shipped in the same carton: 36 pieces, 81 x 39.5 x 87.5 cm, 0.28 CBM, 29.2 kg gross, 0.81 kg per unit. The difference is the minimum. At 180 pieces this needs five cartons, 1.4 CBM, against the 720 pieces and 20 cartons of the bulb version, at the same $5.65 unit price. For a buyer who has not yet sold a standing bubble unit, that is the whole argument: identical cube per piece, a quarter of the commitment, and the same carton for a later top-up.

Read together, the two standing models answer two different questions. The TF213303 is the trial and the single-silhouette order, and a 20GP holds 100 cartons or 3,600 pieces of it. The TF213301 is the four-colour set with a remote, ordered in six hundreds, for a retailer that wants a matched range on the floor. Because the cartons are identical, a buyer can open with the sunflower and switch the balance of the container to the bulb version on the second order without changing anything about the freight.
visible_features: Sunflower head with a perforated centre, which is where the bubbles come out
Clear bulb-shaped funnel directly under the flower head
Green pole with a coloured joint band, standing in a round green base
Bubbles released at lawn height and carried forward, not straight up
Same carton as the TF213301: 36 pieces, 0.28 CBM, 0.81 kg per piece
Single green colourway

TF213249.headline: A crown, wings and a jewel, on a wand
overview: The TF213249 is the only hand-held item in this collection. The head is a gold crown sitting above jewelled heart panels, flanked by pink fairy wings moulded in a translucent plastic with a star pattern, and the wing line continues to the collar. Below that the handle tapers down in pink to a gold band and ends in a faceted gem that matches the head. It is supplied with its own bottle of bubble water, a faceted pink bottle with a screw cap, so the packaging is a gift-ready pair rather than a unit that needs fluid bought separately. The model name specifies music, and the light runs through the head and the translucent wings.

Two colours are mixed in every carton, packed two pieces to an inner box, which means a retailer never has to choose between the colourways to place an order. A carton holds 48 pieces at 0.222 CBM and 25 kg gross, 0.52 kg per unit, so 24 inner boxes of two. The 240-piece minimum is five cartons, 0.222 CBM each, and a 20GP takes 126 cartons, 6,048 pieces.

This is the impulse item in the range and it is priced to sit at counter height. The wands at $6.18 work next to the standing units rather than competing with them: a garden centre or a toy department that already carries the TF213303 or the TF213301 can add a counter display of wands and pick up the pocket-money purchase that a $5.65 floor unit does not get. For a buyer whose channel is gift shops or party retail, the wand is often the first order and the standing models the second.
visible_features: Gold crown finial above jewelled heart panels in the head
Translucent pink fairy wings with a moulded star pattern
Tapered pink handle with a gold collar and a faceted gem at the base
Own bottle of bubble water supplied, faceted pink with a screw cap
Two colours mixed in every carton, packed two pieces to an inner box
Carton packed 48 pieces, 0.52 kg per piece gross
